# hyperfluid_backup_target (Resource)

Where managed PostgreSQL databases send their backups: a bucket of the environment (`bucket_name`) or an external S3-compatible endpoint.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "hyperfluid_environment" "default" {
  name = "default"
}

# Backup-target credentials are referenced by secret NAME, never inline. Create
# the secrets first (here from sensitive variables, so the values never land in
# the Terraform config or state) and reference them by name below.
variable "backup_access_key_id" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "backup_secret_access_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "hyperfluid_secret" "backup_access_key" {
  name             = "backup-access-key"
  secret_type      = "plaintext"
  value            = var.backup_access_key_id
  value_wo_version = "1"
}

resource "hyperfluid_secret" "backup_secret_key" {
  name             = "backup-secret-key"
  secret_type      = "plaintext"
  value            = var.backup_secret_access_key
  value_wo_version = "1"
}

# The target only becomes Ready after the operator probes the endpoint
# (HeadBucket + write/read/list/delete), so endpoint_url, destination_path, and
# the credentials must point at a bucket that already exists and is writable.
# Note: insecure = true is not supported with an https:// endpoint — use http://
# or a trusted TLS cert.
resource "hyperfluid_backup_target" "offsite" {
  env          = data.hyperfluid_environment.default.id
  name         = "offsite"
  endpoint_url = "https://s3.eu-west-3.amazonaws.com"
  # Bucket + an arbitrary prefix to store backups under (NOT a database name);
  # each cluster's backups are laid out beneath it as <prefix>/<server>/...
  destination_path              = "s3://my-backups/hyperfluid/"
  access_key_secret_name        = hyperfluid_secret.backup_access_key.name
  secret_access_key_secret_name = hyperfluid_secret.backup_secret_key.name
  # How long base backups and WAL archives are kept, 1-35 days. Left out, the
  # platform keeps 7.
  retention_days = 14
}

# Or back up into a bucket of the environment: the platform resolves its
# endpoint and credentials, and reports what it resolved in endpoint_url and
# destination_path. Moving a target between a bucket and an external endpoint
# replaces it.
resource "hyperfluid_bucket" "pg_backups" {
  env  = data.hyperfluid_environment.default.id
  name = "pg-backups"
}

resource "hyperfluid_backup_target" "in_environment" {
  env         = data.hyperfluid_environment.default.id
  name        = "in-environment"
  bucket_name = hyperfluid_bucket.pg_backups.name
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `env` (String) Environment id the target belongs to. Changing this forces a new target.
- `name` (String) Backup target name (slug). Changing this forces a new target.

### Optional

- `access_key_secret_name` (String) Name of the secret holding the S3 access key id. Required without `bucket_name`.
- `bucket_name` (String) Name of an existing bucket of the environment to back up into. Conflicts with the external endpoint attributes. Changing this forces a new target.
- `description` (String) Free-form description.
- `destination_path` (String) Bucket and prefix, e.g. `s3://backups/`. Required without `bucket_name`.
- `endpoint_url` (String) S3-compatible endpoint URL, e.g. `https://s3.eu-west-3.amazonaws.com`. Required without `bucket_name`.
- `insecure` (Boolean) Skip TLS verification of the endpoint, for development only. Not available with `bucket_name`. Changing this forces a new target.
- `retention_days` (Number) How many days backups are kept, 1 to 35. Defaults to 7.
- `secret_access_key_secret_name` (String) Name of the secret holding the S3 secret access key. Required without `bucket_name`.
- `tags` (List of String) User-defined tags.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `phase` (String) Current lifecycle phase.
- `slug` (String) Derived slug.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Backup target import id is the backup target id (uuid).
terraform import hyperfluid_backup_target.offsite 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
